newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia buys Wassum Investment Network.
newsitem.headline: Skandia buys Wassum Investment Network.

text.p: STOCKHOLM, Oct 17 (Rueter) - Swedish insurance company Skandia on Thursday said it had acquired Wassum Investment Network AB so that it can better meet the requirements of specialist client groups.
The company said the chief executive of Wassum, Leif Passmark, formerly head of SkandiaLink, would return to Skandia where he will work to develop market strategy.
Passmark will report directly to Lars-Eric Petersson, recently appointed president and chief executive officer of Skandia with effect from January 1, 1997.
"In order to promote operations further in the areas of savings products, Skandia will purchase all the shares in Wassum Investment Network AB," Skandia said in a statement.
No financial details of the deal were provided.
Skandia said Wassum's operations were directed towards the long-term savings market to which retirement pensions contribute an important part.

"Wassum, which will be an independent subsidiary within the Skandia group, will make an important contribution to Skandia's continued efforts to develop further in new markets," Petersson said in the statement.
